title: review Skill Schema
description: Input/output format for resume quality evaluation. The review skill performs pure diagnosis: it scores the resume across multiple dimensions and produces a list of concrete, actionable issues. It does NOT modify the resume.

resume.description: The resume markdown to evaluate. Can come from any source (user-written, AI-generated, output of other skills).

jd.description: Optional: target job description. When provided, the skill evaluates the jdMatch dimension by checking each key requirement against the resume.

sourceTexts.description: Optional: original source materials (e.g. raw user inputs, dig conversation transcripts). When provided, the skill performs anti-hallucination checks and evaluates the truthfulness dimension.

pdfText.description: Optional: raw text extracted from the resume's PDF (the rendered text layer). When provided, the skill runs the ATS / parseability check (broken/split tokens, stray hyphens, ligature artifacts, bilingual keyword duplication). ATS cannot be assessed from markdown alone, so omit this when no PDF text is available.

language.description: Output language for issue descriptions, suggestions, and summary.

score.description: Overall quality score (weighted average of dimensions). Two decimals. When truthfulness < 0.5, score is capped at 0.5 regardless of other dimensions.

expression.description: How vivid, action-oriented, quantified, and concrete the language is.

structure.description: Whether the section ordering, focus, and length allocation are reasonable.

credibility.description: Whether claims are backed by concrete facts (numbers, tech stack, deliverables) and internally consistent.

jdMatch.description: Only present when jd is provided. Score equals the proportion of JD key requirements covered by the resume (partial coverage counts as 0.5).

truthfulness.description: Only present when sourceTexts is provided. Measures whether resume facts/numbers can be traced back to source materials. Fabrications drive this dimension toward 0.

ats.description: Only present when pdfText is provided. Parseability of the resume's text layer for ATS: no broken/split tokens, no stray hyphens, no ligature artifacts, no unintended keyword duplication from a bilingual text layer.

issues.description: Concrete issues sorted from most to least severe. Truthfulness issues come first, then jdMatch gaps, then severe credibility/expression/structure issues, then minor optimizations.

type.description: Which dimension this issue belongs to.

location.description: Specific location in the resume (e.g. 'Work Experience - Alibaba - bullet 3', 'Education first line'). Use '全文' / 'whole resume' only for global issues.

problem.description: Concrete description of what is wrong. Must not be vague (avoid 'expression is bad'); be specific.

suggestion.description: Actionable fix. Must specify HOW to fix (e.g. 'add concrete numbers like QPS and P99 latency'), not vague advice like 'write better'.

summary.description: 2-3 sentence overall assessment covering key strengths and the most important areas for improvement. May suggest downstream skills (polish / dig / generate) when appropriate.
